name: Respiratory variants & flu
value: US flu admissions 7x last year; severity low
summary: US flu admissions hit 9,584 in the week to 7 Nov, over seven times a year earlier; CDC still rates severity low
state: CDC reported 9,584 flu hospital admissions in the week to 7 Nov, up 14% on the week and more than seven times the same week of 2025, with seven jurisdictions at high or very high activity and severity still rated low (CDC; Becker's, 16 Nov). The CDC estimates at least 2,100 flu deaths so far this season, including five children (Becker's). Searches on 18 Nov found no new WHO variant designation and no health systems reported as strained, so an unusually early US season keeps Watch.
for_you: The NHS offers free flu vaccines to eligible groups, including over-65s, young children and people with some health conditions. UKHSA publishes weekly flu and COVID-19 surveillance.
rubric_hit: Watch: a hemisphere's flu season unusually early (US admissions 9,584 in week to 7 Nov, 7x last year); no variant of concern, no systems strained

sources.title: CDC — Weekly US Influenza Surveillance Report, week 44 ending 7 November 2026
Becker's Hospital Review — Flu admissions running more than 7x higher than last year

why: Known viruses change; a new COVID-19 variant or a severe flu strain can strain health systems without being 'novel'.
drivers: Viral evolution, waning immunity, seasonal patterns, vaccine match.

rubric.alert: WHO designates a variant of concern, or flu or COVID-19 hospitalisations strain several countries' health systems.
rubric.watch: WHO designates a new variant of interest, or a hemisphere's flu season is unusually early or severe.
rubric.normal: No WHO variant of interest rising fast; flu seasons of normal severity.
